name: second-brain-eval-tooling
description: Out-of-band tooling for the evaluation work. NOT part of the app and NOT part of the Node eval path — see the comment block below.
_why: backend/package.json carries the app and nothing else, and the Node eval
dependency-free — it requires only Node builtins, which is what keeps a
transitive version bump from moving an nDCG.
Phase 3.4 needs an embedding model, which is a heavy native dependency. It
goes HERE rather than in backend/package.json, mirroring exactly what 2.4
did with scripts/.venv + scripts/requirements.txt for pytrec_eval: the
tooling that produces or certifies an artifact lives outside the package
whose dependency list is a claim.
EVALUATION.md §7.1 draws the line this respects: embedding is corpus
PREPARATION, not part of the retriever. The vectors are written to a file
and handed to v5-embeddings as data. backend/tests/retrieval.interface.js
enforces the other half mechanically — nothing under backend/retrieval/ may
require anything outside it, `crypto` excepted — so this dependency cannot
reach the retriever even by accident.
PINNED BY LOCKFILE, NOT BY RANGE. package-lock.json is committed and carries
a per-package integrity hash; install with `npm ci`, never `npm install`.
That is the npm analogue of requirements.txt's --require-hashes and of
1.6's image digest: a range names a name, a hash names bytes.

scripts.postinstall: node -e "console.log('scripts/: install with npm ci, not npm install — the lockfile is the pin')"
